Since no corner of the small square is marked as the center of the original paper (the folds are along two adjacent sides of the small square, meeting at the center), the cut is placed on a "free" corner (a corner formed by the outer edges of the original paper).
4.  **Unfolding:**
    *   The cut corner corresponds to the center of the folded structure but is located at the midpoint of the side of the original large square.
    *   When unfolded once, the cut creates a shape on the edge of the rectangle.
    *   When unfolded a second time, the four "edge-midpoints" of the large square are revealed to have identical notches.
5.  **Matching with Options:**
    *   Option (A) shows a hole in the center.
    *   Option (B) shows notches on the four midpoints of the square's sides. This matches our deduction.
